title: Python async (asyncio), Part 9: seeing and testing async code
tldr: A request that waits forever raises nothing, logs nothing and uses no CPU: measured on gateway v9, an audit store that stops answering leaves 5 shoppers with no answer, 0 log lines, a green per-seller dashboard and 0 ms of loop lag. The tools, each run on that incident: debug mode, which times callbacks and so sees blocking but not waiting; asyncio.all_tasks() and Task.get_stack(), one frame per Task; Python 3.14's call graph (format_call_graph, capture_call_graph) with each Task's whole await chain and who awaits it; python -m asyncio ps and pstree from outside the process, and the permissions they need; and loop lag as a metric. Gateway v10 adds seller and request histograms that include every outcome, JSON log lines with the request id, Tasks named by shopper, a 1 s limit on the audit wait and a task dump on SIGUSR1, and runs unchanged on uvloop. Tests replace the sellers at one seam, run the pools inline and use a loop whose clock jumps to the next timer, so the 250 ms budget, a hang-up, Part 8's shutdown report and a stalled store are asserted exactly in milliseconds. Then flaky tests (real sleeps, leaked Tasks, shared loops), a call-graph bug in Python 3.14.0 to 3.14.7, metrics that lie, telemetry at 10 times the load, what to page on, a comparison of testing approaches, an observability checklist and an interview drill.
